steps.title: Network Discovery
steps.description: Explore the network interfaces of your sandbox. It has no route to the internet, so the loopback interface is where everything in this lab happens.
tasks: List your network interfaces and their addresses: `ip -o addr show` (if `ip` is not installed, `ifconfig` shows the same information)
Save that output to a file: `ip -o addr show > ~/interfaces.txt`
Find the loopback interface and its address in the file: `grep 127.0.0.1 ~/interfaces.txt`

verification.command: grep -Eq '(^|[ :])lo0?[ :]' /home/student/interfaces.txt && grep -q '127\.0\.0\.1' /home/student/interfaces.txt && echo PASS || echo FAIL

steps.title: Name Resolution
steps.description: See how a name is turned into an IP address: the local hosts table is checked first, then the DNS servers listed in the resolver configuration.
tasks: See which DNS servers this machine would ask: `cat /etc/resolv.conf`
Read the local hosts table, which is checked before DNS: `cat /etc/hosts`
Resolve a name the way programs do: `getent hosts localhost`
Save the answer to a file: `getent hosts localhost > ~/dns.txt`

verification.command: grep -q 'localhost' /home/student/dns.txt && grep -Eq '127\.0\.0\.1|::1' /home/student/dns.txt && echo PASS || echo FAIL

steps.title: HTTP Requests with curl
steps.description: Start a small web server on the loopback interface, then make HTTP requests to it and inspect the responses like a pro.
tasks:
Create a page to serve: `mkdir -p ~/site && echo '

Hello from OpsAcademy

' > ~/site/index.html`
Start a web server for that folder in the background: `python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory ~/site > ~/server.log 2>&1 &`
Save the response body to a file: `curl -s http://localhost:8000/ -o ~/response.html`
See the requests the server logged: `cat ~/server.log`

verification.command: cmp -s /home/student/site/index.html /home/student/response.html && grep -q 'HEAD / HTTP' /home/student/server.log && grep -q 'GET / HTTP' /home/student/server.log && echo PASS || echo FAIL

steps.title: Listening Ports
steps.description: Check which ports are open and what services are listening, then shut your web server down and confirm its port has closed.
tasks: Save the list while your web server is still running: `ss -tln > ~/ports.txt`
Find your server's port in it: `grep 8000 ~/ports.txt`
Stop the server: `kill %1` (or find its PID with `ps aux | grep '[h]ttp.server'` and run `kill <PID>`)
Confirm nothing answers on the port any more: `curl -s -m 2 http://localhost:8000/ || echo closed`

verification.command: grep -Eq '[:.]8000([^0-9]|$)' /home/student/ports.txt && ! curl -s -o /dev/null -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:8000/ && echo PASS || echo FAIL
